proposed_fix.description: Confirm network loss on the node/pod hosting checkoutservice, then, with approval, move checkoutservice to a different node and revert if there is no improvement.
steps: Identify the pod(s) and node(s) running checkoutservice (kubectl get pod -o wide) and check whether other pods on that node show similar network symptoms.
On that node, inspect interface receive/transmit errors and drops (ip -s link, ethtool -S, node_network_receive_errs_total) to confirm packet loss.
Check node conntrack usage versus its limit (R3 diagnostic step only) to rule out table exhaustion as the cause of drops.
Review checkoutservice resource usage given the memory and socket increases in E4 (mem z=6.26, socket z=6.69), and look for connection buildup.
If loss is confirmed on the node, after human approval cordon that node and delete/reschedule one checkoutservice pod onto a healthy node (R1 'spread services to other nodes/pods').
Watch checkoutservice latency-50/90 and frontend error rates for recovery; scale replicas back or uncordon if no improvement.
preconditions: Confirm checkoutservice has more than one replica or tolerates a restart, so rescheduling does not cause an outage.
Confirm a healthy node has spare cpu/memory capacity to host the pod.
Get on-call approval before cordoning or deleting any pod.
Verify that the node-level network errors or drops actually exist before moving workloads.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node and, if needed, reschedule the pod or scale back to the original placement; no persistent node settings are changed by this plan.
